MF9 structure. (1) A pure guard in front of an injected transport: every request passes Guard.check(method, path, body) before it is sent, and a refused request is never sent; the writer's operations (branch, fast-forward update, commit, pull request, check, merge, revert) are thin calls through it. One rule set then judges the writer, the vectors (python -m target.write guard PLAN) and any later caller (MF10 ledger.append, MF13 gate.revert, MF18 activate), instead of a check per operation. (2) A closed route list, not a deny list: 11 routes under /repos/<owner>/<repo>/ of one repository; the contents API, the merges endpoint, ref deletion, repository settings, GraphQL and other repositories are refused because they are not listed, so a route nobody thought of is refused too. Blobs and trees are left out until their first caller (MF10, Y4). (3) Merge is guarded by what the guard saw: only a pull request seen open in a response, base and head under brain/, head sha pinned, merge_method merge (two parents, so the revert rule can read the first parent). (4) Revert: only the head of the branch, only a two-parent commit; tree = first parent's tree, one parent (the merge); it goes onto a brain/c/ branch and through a pull request, because brain/integration takes no direct push (tohum/01b), so the revert passes the gate like a candidate (tohum/07). (5) The HTTPS transport follows no redirect: urllib would carry the Authorization header and a POST turned GET to the Location host. deps_npm already does the same (_NoRedirect); I did not merge the two classes: deps_npm raises its own DepsError inside the getir job and target.write returns an ApiError in yaz, and one shared three-line class across two jobs with different error types is the wrong abstraction. (6) One way, tested structurally: no referee module except target/write.py names a github.com host or a push/send-pack command, and only target/write.py and runner/deps_npm.py import a network module; deps_npm is checked to open bare URLs only (no Request, data, method or headers).

(3) Lines are git lines, not ESLint's: measured with real ESLint 10.13.0, ESLint counts a lone CR and U+2028/2029 as line breaks and gives columns and fix ranges in UTF-16 units of the text without its BOM; the converter maps every position to an offset and counts only LF, so the gate's mapped line and scope rule see the same lines as the diff. (4) Suppressed messages are violations (gate/check.py's own note): measured end to end, a real eslint-disable-next-line candidate is not_distinguished with them and merges without them. (5) A parse error (ruleId null, fatal) refuses the run: its file's violations vanish, which would lower the ratchet count. (6) A non-fatal message with no rule id (unused directive) gets the reserved id eslint:no-rule-id. (7) fix range: first = line of the start; last = line of the last replaced unit, or the next line when that unit is LF and the new text does not end with LF (the next line is joined).
